title: Buffered Evacuation Resilience Controller for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a controller that coordinates GPU pool drains with the autoscaler by maintaining a live buffer of preservable capacity slices. The controller should enable staged evacuation windows with rollbackable gates tied to LTS rollout policies and runtime compatibility checks, so upgrades can proceed without violating capacity SLOs or causing tenant impact spikes.
design_notes: We observed tail latency spikes and transient error rates during previous upgrades when the autoscaler and drain operations competed for the same allocation budget. The proposed controller maintains an ephemeral reservation (buffer slices) that are drained first and can be reattached or rebalanced depending on demand. Key design elements: 1) soft-buffer allocation per pool that autoscaler recognizes as non-evictable until gating signal; 2) phased evacuation phases (pre-drain verification, soft-drain, hard-drain); 3) rollout gate hooks (canary pass/fail, QA traffic validation) exposed to Console for human overrides; 4) fallbacks to compatible model-variants or cross-region routing if local capacity falls under threshold. Controller should be pluggable into existing pool-operator and expose metrics for the console rollout dashboard.
implementation_steps: Spec controller API: signals, phases, and buffer lifecycle
Extend pool allocator: add buffer slice primitives and tagging for autoscaler to honor
Autoscaler contract changes: honor buffer reservations and expose predicted headroom metrics
Integrate rollout-gates: wire canary/QA pass signals into controller decision loop
Add reconciliation loop: enforce phased progression and retries with backoff
End-to-end e2e tests in staging with synthetic tenant traffic
Feature flag and gradual enablement across a subset of pools
test_plan: Unit tests for buffer lifecycle and state transitions
Integration tests with autoscaler in CI to validate honor/non-evict semantics
Staging upgrade run: compare tokenized QPS and p95 latency vs baseline during drain
Chaos test: random autoscaler mispredictions and sudden tenant surges to validate soft-fallbacks
Canary rollout to 3 low-impact pools then to 30% of dedicated fleet
Post-rollout evaluation against rollout gate metrics (errors, latency, backlog)
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO: no more than 2% tenant request failures attributable to upgrade during rollout
Dashboard: rollout-gate timeline with buffer headroom overlay
Pager: on-call paging for pool-level loss of capacity or runaway evictions
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deployment: controller disabled by default
Enable read-only mode in staging and validate metrics emission
Enable active mode on canary pools (low-util dedicated pools) for 48h
Run a controlled LTS upgrade against canaries with QA traffic and gate checks
If canary stable, progressively enable on 10% fleet, then 50%, then global
Rollback path: controller exposes immediate abort which reattaches buffers and signals autoscaler to reallocate
Post-mortem window: 72h monitoring and automatic pause if SLO regressions detected
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: autoscaler ignores buffer semantics and preemptively scales down -> Mitigation: autoscaler contract change and staged enforcement with a feature flag
Risk: buffer reservations reduce usable capacity causing denial for bursty tenants -> Mitigation: dynamic buffer sizing tied to moving-average headroom and tenant-priority overrides
Risk: rollout gate misconfiguration stalls upgrades -> Mitigation: default conservative gates, manual overrides in Console, and canary rollouts
Risk: cross-region routing introduces latency/regulatory issues -> Mitigation: only enable cross-region fallback for non-sensitive workloads and require policy allow-list
open_questions: How should multi-tenant priority credits be consumed when buffers are active? (preempt lower-priority low-cost tenants first?)
What is the canonical visibility surface in Console for buffer slices and per-tenant expected disruption?
Should buffer reservations be persisted across control-plane restarts or recomputed on reconcile?
Do we need a hard quota for maximum buffer percent per pool to avoid starvation?
